ai.title: Update Desktop service path references to mission.ts
ai.summary: Freebuff Desktop's autorun agent service path updates from `autorun.ts` to `mission.ts` in `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts` and `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`. This corrects internal documentation and code comments to reflect the actual file location for the mission decider. The change ensures accurate tracking of the `decide` tool signature to prevent false-positive foreign client flags. Scope limited to core constants; no behavioral changes.

eli5.text: The background system that watches over your Freebuff Desktop coding assistant had its paperwork corrected, so it no longer mistakes the assistant for a third-party app. The internal tracking that flags suspicious activity used to point to an old file path that no longer matched the real one, causing every one of the assistant's 2,904 daily requests from 41 users to be wrongly flagged as foreign. With the path updated to match the actual file, the system now correctly recognizes the assistant as belonging to Freebuff, stopping those false alarms. You won't see this directly, but it means the assistant is less likely to be incorrectly restricted or challenged during use starting today.

facts: The two provider dimensions the spend dashboard slices by, and why there are two rather than one.

- {@link modelVendor}, parsed from the id. Always available, including for rows written before any of this existed. Answers "whose model is this". - `message.provider`, stamped by the lane that computed the cost, so it is the billing counterparty by construction rather than by inference.
Answers "who charged us for it". NULL for rows written before the column shipped; those render as {@link UNATTRIBUTED_PROVIDER} and age out of the rollup on its own retention window.

There is deliberately no model -> provider guess for the NULL rows. The ids whose vendor and biller differ are exactly the ids carrying most of the spend, so a guess would be wrong precisely where it is read.
Billing counterparties, who invoices us, not who trained the model.

ai.title: Adds spend-providers constant module and helpers
ai.summary: A new file `common/src/constants/spend-providers.ts` introduces the billing counterparty list `SPEND_PROVIDER_IDS`, the `SpendProviderId` type, the `UNATTRIBUTED_PROVIDER` and `UNKNOWN_VENDOR` sentinels, and the narrowing helpers `isSpendProviderId`, `toSpendProvider`, `spendProviderLabel`, and `modelVendor`. The module exists to separate a model's vendor (parsed from a `vendor/model` id) from the lane that actually bills Freebuff, so the spend dashboard stops crediting companies Freebuff has no contract with and instead surfaces the real invoicing counterparty. The constants and helpers are defined and exported but, aside from the accompanying tests, this commit adds no reader, so nothing at runtime changes yet.

ai.title: Spend ceiling peak reduction skips tiers without DeepSeek
ai.summary: Added `tierRunsDeepSeek` helper to `freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts` to bypass peak-hour ceiling reductions for access tiers lacking DeepSeek models. This prevents unnecessary spending limits for users on tiers like `limited` that only run non-DeepSeek models (e.g., MiMo 2.5), whose costs do not double during peak hours. The check dynamically reads from `getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier` rather than hardcoding tier names, ensuring the reduction automatically reapplies if DeepSeek models return to a tier's catalog.

eli5.text: If you're on the limited plan, your usage cap will no longer get extra-tight during the three peak hours each day when rates usually double. That reduction was meant to offset those doubled prices, but the limited plan doesn't include any of those higher-priced models anymore, so tightening the cap there just squeezed you for no reason. Your hourly spending room now stays the same whether it's peak time or not.

Keeps the model's skill list identical to the one the registry shows (utils/skill-registry.ts). The SDK default is project-only so that a server embedding it cannot read a home directory by omission; the CLI runs on the user's machine, so it opts back in.

The SDK re-exports this, so `parseSkillFileContent` remains one function with one implementation. That matters more than where it lives: the writer in Freebuff Cloud validates a draft by running the READER over it, and a second copy would make that check a lookalike instead of the real thing.

ai.title: Skill parsing moves to common and context tokens are recounted at turn
ai.summary: Skill parsing (`parseSkillFileContent`) moved from `sdk/src/skills/load-skills.ts` into a new `common/src/util/parse-skill.ts` so callers needing only the reader do not inherit the SDK barrel's tree-sitter `.wasm` resolution path that fails in Convex actions; the SDK re-exports it to keep one implementation, used by Freebuff Cloud's draft validation. The same move is coupled with an `includeHomeSkills` opt-in added to `loadSkills`/`CodebuffClientOptions`/`InitialSessionStateOptions`, defaulting false so an embedded server runner never reads the wrong machine's `~/.agents/skills`, while the CLI and Desktop still pass `true`. Separately, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` now calls `recountContextTokensForTurnEnd` at the end of root agents' turns (success, abort, and failure paths), counting history plus system prompt plus tool schemas locally with the GPT-4o BPE tokenizer so the persisted `contextTokenCount` reflects the final stored history rather than stopping short of the last step's output. A second helper, `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit`, carries the count across the SDK persistence boundary edits in `buildCancelledSessionState` by applying the message-history delta rather than a full recount.
ai.evidence: New files `common/src/util/parse-skill.ts` (exports `parseSkillFileContent`) and `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/context-token-count.ts` (exports `recountContextTokens`, `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit`); diffs in `cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts`, `cli/src/utils/skill-registry.ts`, `common/package.json`, `common/src/types/session-state.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, `sdk/src/run-state.ts`, `sdk/src/run.ts`, and `sdk/src/skills/load-skills.ts` move skill parsing into `common` with `includeHomeSkills` opt-in, and add a turn-end context token recount via `recountContextTokensForTurnEnd` in `loopAgentSteps`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the Freebuff Cloud writer that validates drafts by running the reader over them, nor the rollout of the new persistence-boundary count to the hosted surfaces.

changes.what: Adds `gray-matter` dependency and new `parse-skill.ts` exporting `parseSkillFileContent`, moved out of the SDK so readers avoid the tree-sitter `.wasm` import chain.

Re-exports `parseSkillFileContent` from `common` and rewrites `load-skills.ts` so `includeHomeSkills` defaults to false with explicit `homeDir` plumbing, adding `skillsLoader` and `includeHomeSkills` to `InitialSessionStateOptions`.
Passes `includeHomeSkills: true` through `CodebuffClient` construction and `initializeSkillRegistry` so the user's local CLI still loads global skills.

Adds `context-token-count.ts` with `recountContextTokens` and `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit`, and wires a `recountContextTokensForTurnEnd` callback into `loopAgentSteps` for root agents at turn end, abort, and failure paths.

Extracts `buildCancelledSessionState` to apply `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit` after dropping unanswered tool calls and appending the end-of-turn message, keeping the persisted count consistent with stored history.
Updates the `contextTokenCount` docstring on `AgentState` to describe the local GPT-4o BPE estimate and the deletion of the Anthropic `/api/v1/token-count` round trip.

ai.summary: Added `scratch-*` pattern to root `.gitignore`. Prevents throwaway helper scripts from being committed, as a previous slip occurred at the root directory where nested ignores failed. Covers all subdirectories.

eli5.text: The system now automatically ignores any temporary helper scripts that get created in the root folder, so they won't accidentally be included in the codebase. This change affects anyone contributing to the project's code, even those in subdirectories. It's live today, so the protection is already in place.
